projects.name: Aurem
projects.description: Online class excludes whoever cannot hear.

highlights.why: Three roles write to the same classroom state at once. Under Context every transcribed sentence re-rendered the whole tree.
Annotation had to travel as vector. As an image it did not fit the socket and went blurry on zoom.
A caption that lags is useless. The budget ran from speech to text on screen, and polling spent it on the round-trip alone.
The caption sits on top of PowerPoint without stealing the presenter click.
Transcribing on the client cut one server round-trip per sentence and kept audio off the wire.

projects.x_detail: Live captioning with the Web Speech API, a collaborative whiteboard in Fabric.js, and an Electron client whose transparent overlay captions on top of any software.
projects.x_problem: Hybrid and remote classes assume everyone can hear. Someone with hearing loss depends on an interpreter in the room or on the captions the video player generates, and those are gone the moment the teacher presents from PowerPoint, from a PDF, or from anything outside the browser.
projects.x_built: An ecosystem on three fronts: an LMS for institutions, a virtual classroom with live captioning, and a desktop client that captions on top of any application.
projects.x_result: It served more than a thousand students and won the Santander Award. The company closed in 2023, but the product ran five years in production while I worked on other teams.

projects.name: Maincore
projects.description: Institutional site that has to sell two technical product lines and capture qualified leads.

highlights.why: The CSS ships inside the server HTML. Without it the first paint arrives unstyled, and this page is the first commercial contact the company gets.

highlights.call: Radix for the accordion and the menu
highlights.why: Product specs live in accordions. Keyboard, focus and ARIA out of the box cost less than reimplementing them wrong.
The token only counts once the backend confirms it with Google. Validating on the client is decorative.

highlights.call: Own SMTP instead of a form service
highlights.why: The lead lands straight in the company mailbox, with no third party holding customer data.
Polaris and Sirius on separate URLs instead of tabs. A product that has to rank needs its own address.

projects.x_detail: Next.js 13 with styled-components on the server, Radix for the interactive components, and lead capture with the captcha verified in the backend.
projects.x_problem: Maincore sells embedded systems and programmable logic, which nobody buys on impulse. The site had to explain two separate product lines, hold up in Portuguese and English search, and turn a visit into a conversation without an intermediary holding the lead data.
projects.x_built: An institutional site in Next.js with two product pages, a resource centre, a contact form and a newsletter signup behind a captcha.
projects.x_result: Live since 2023 on Vercel, two product lines documented, and the form delivering straight to the company mailbox.
projects.x_retrospective: Translation is decided on the client by navigator.language, and the html lang attribute is hardcoded to "en". A crawler never sees the English version and the declared language does not match the content. Today I would use a route per locale, which is what I did on this portfolio with next-intl.

projects.name: This portfolio
projects.description: Developer portfolios assert competence. This one tries to prove it.

highlights.call: Sentry in Terraform, not the dashboard
highlights.why: Production alerting is infrastructure. In code it goes through review and keeps its history, and a Go contract test checks the rule before apply.
This is a public repo that deploys infrastructure. A secret leaked in an old commit is still leaked, so scanning the diff alone does nothing.
Tags are mutable, SHAs are not. Dependabot proposes the bump and I review it.

highlights.call: The Terraform plan never lands on a PR
highlights.why: The check status is public, the plan is not. A plan exposes production topology in an open pull request.

highlights.call: Serialized apply in a protected environment
highlights.why: It runs only on protected master, after every check, inside a GitHub production environment.
Accessibility that does not run in the pipeline rots on the first tight sprint.
No analytics fires before the visitor chooses.

projects.x_detail: Feature-based architecture with MVVM, unit, e2e and a11y tests running in CI, i18n, consent and Sentry. It ships through GitHub Actions with Terraform.
projects.x_problem: An engineer portfolio usually lists technology. Listing proves nothing: the repository is public, so the way to prove it is to leave the process visible.
projects.x_built: Next.js with a feature-based architecture and MVVM, i18n by route, consent before any event, and the observability infrastructure described in Terraform.
projects.x_result: ADR 0001 records the threat model of a public repository that deploys. The end-to-end suites cover accessibility and privacy, and CodeQL runs on pull requests, on master and once a week. The pipeline that ships this site is the same one you can read in the repository.
